body:
We make Kiron, so weigh this accordingly. Everything here about Hevy comes from its App Store listing, help center and website, checked November 15, 2026. Everything about Kiron describes version 1.2.

Hevy is a very good workout log: quick, free to start, and rated 4.9 from about 104,000 ratings on the US App Store. Kiron (that's us) does a different job. It plans your training for you. Here's how to tell which one you need.

Hevy or Kiron? The quick verdict

  • Choose Kiron if you'd rather follow a plan than write one. Pick a proven program, or paste the one you have, and Kiron plans each workout, suggests your weights with a note saying why, keeps the next workout ready whenever you train, and puts your runs on the same calendar.
  • Stay with Hevy if you'd rather build your own routines, you like a social feed, or you log from an Apple Watch or Wear OS watch.
  • Switching is easy: Kiron imports your Hevy history.

Bottom line: Hevy logs well and costs less; its Pro plan is $23.99 a year, against Kiron's {{kiron:price-annual}}. Kiron costs more because it does the planning, and if you'd rather follow a program than manage one, we think that's worth paying for.

What Kiron is

Kiron is a workout app for {{kiron:cell-platforms}} that plans your training from a program. You can start three ways:

  • Choose one of {{kiron:program-count}} ready-made programs by goal: strength, muscle, home workouts, running or a mix.
  • Answer a few questions, and Kiron builds one for you.
  • Bring your own plan. Paste it from ChatGPT, a coach or a website, or snap a photo, and it becomes a program you can follow.

From then on, Kiron handles the details:

  • The next workout is always ready, on set days or whenever you get to the gym.
  • First-time weights come with a reason. Kiron suggests one for every lift, a short note explains it, and a "How did it feel?" check after a set adjusts the rest.
  • Weights rise as you get stronger, and Kiron tells you why.
  • Variety that keeps your main lifts: smaller exercises can change week to week while the big lifts stay.
  • Travel gyms: save a hotel or garage gym with its equipment, and Kiron swaps in exercises that fit.
  • Runs and race plans on the same calendar as your lifting, from a first 5K to a marathon or a sprint triathlon.
  • Recovery that counts your other workouts, like runs and rides other apps save to Apple Health or Health Connect.
  • {{kiron:progress-lead}} {{kiron:progress-detail}} {{kiron:progress-import}}
  • {{kiron:offline-lead}} {{kiron:offline-detail}}
  • The price: {{kiron:pricing-sentence}}

Many follow formats lifters and runners have used for decades, like Beginner 5×5, Push / Pull / Legs and Half Marathon.

Logging a program vs having it planned

Hevy's pitch is a fast log that stays out of your way. You build routines (each one a saved workout) or copy them from Hevy's library or other lifters. At the gym you start one, and Hevy shows last time's weights and reps as you log. Friends can follow along in a feed.

We know that way of training. For many years our founding team ran a push/pull/legs program (pushing muscles one day, pulling the next, then legs) in Strong, a log much like Hevy, simply doing the next day of the program at each visit. It works.

Kiron keeps that rhythm. It's like following a program in a log, except the planning and the progress are done for you:

  • The next workout is waiting. In Kiron's Whenever I train mode, a program has no dates: open the app, and the next workout is up. Nothing is ever marked missed, two workouts in a day is fine, and you can set a weekly target ("aim for 4 a week"). Prefer a schedule? Fixed days puts workouts on your calendar and can move missed ones forward.
  • Weights you don't have to guess. Every lift starts with a weight: from your history (a little lighter after time away) or from a related lift you've logged. A short note says which, like "You did 100 lb × 8 on EZ Bar Curl, so we started Hammer Curl at 35 lb per hand." After a set, Kiron asks "How did 35 lb feel?" and adjusts the sets still to come. When you hit every set, the weight goes up next time, and Kiron says so.
  • Runs planned alongside lifting. Hevy logs cardio with time and distance. Kiron plans it: running programs from Beginner 5K to Marathon, plus Sprint Triathlon and Run + Lift, sit on the same calendar as your lifting, and the recovery map counts both. Here's how to space running and lifting in one week.
  • A plan from anywhere. To follow a coach's or ChatGPT's plan in Hevy, you type it in as routines (more on ChatGPT below). In Kiron, you paste the text or snap a photo, check how each exercise matched, and the plan lands on your schedule, phases and all.

Both apps show last time's numbers as you log, handle warm-up sets, run a rest timer, track personal records and let you swap one exercise for another.

What about Hevy Trainer?

Hevy's Pro plan includes Hevy Trainer, a program builder that deserves a fair look. You answer questions about your goal, experience, equipment, and how often and how long you can train. It builds a lifting program with workouts, exercises, rep targets, rest times and suggested starting weights, raises the weights as you log, and shows your next scheduled workout. Updates since July added exercise swaps, help working around injuries, more ways to split the week and an option to include cardio. Hevy calls it algorithm-based, not AI.

So if you want an app to write and progress a lifting program, and you're happy in Hevy, Trainer does that for $23.99 a year. Kiron's case is where your plan can come from (a proven program, a running or race plan, or the plan you already have), with runs and recovery alongside your lifting.

The App Store lists two monthly prices for Hevy Pro, and we couldn't confirm which one a new subscriber sees. Prices vary by country and offer.

Hevy's free plan logs unlimited workouts with no ads, but holds 4 routines, 7 custom exercises and 3 months of history, according to its help center. A routine is one saved workout, so a plan with five different workouts needs Pro. Workouts are capped at 150 sets, even on Pro, though Hevy says most never come close.

Paying monthly, Kiron is {{kiron:price-monthly}}, or {{kiron:price-monthly-yearly}} if you keep it all year, so if you're staying, the yearly plan is the one to compare.

Moving from Hevy, history and all

  1. Export from Hevy. Go to Profile, Settings, Export & Import Data, Export Data, and choose Export Workouts. You get a spreadsheet file (CSV). Our guide to exporting your workout history covers other apps too.
  2. Start Kiron. Pick a program or paste your plan, and choose fixed days or Whenever I train.
  3. Bring your history. In Kiron's Settings, tap Import from another app and choose the file. Kiron shows how each exercise matched before saving, and you can remove an import later. Finished workouts come over; Hevy routines don't.
  4. Train. For lifts in your Hevy history, Kiron starts from your recent numbers. For anything new, it suggests a weight, says why, and asks how it felt.

Who should stay with Hevy

  • A free log is all you need. If you write your own routines and four of them cover your week, Hevy's free plan logs unlimited workouts with no ads. Kiron has no free version.
  • You want planning for less. Hevy Pro, Trainer included, is $23.99 a year or $74.99 once; Kiron is {{kiron:price-annual}}.
  • Friends keep you going. Hevy's feed lets you follow friends, see their workouts and compare lifts. Kiron has no feed; you can share a workout by link or as a picture.
  • You log from your wrist. Hevy has Apple Watch and Wear OS apps. Kiron has neither, and reads heart rate from Apple Health or Health Connect after a workout.
  • Videos help you learn. Hevy shows a video and step-by-step instructions for its exercises; most of Kiron's have an animated demo.
  • You want your data portable. Hevy exports your workouts as a file and also runs in a web browser. Kiron has no export and no web version.
  • You value a long track record. Hevy says more than 18 million people use it. Kiron is new and still small.

Hevy questions, answered

Is Hevy free, and is the free plan enough?

Yes, Hevy is free to use: unlimited workout logging with no ads, within the limits above. If a free log is all you need, stay on it.

Is Hevy Pro worth it?

If you've outgrown 4 routines, want your full history, or want Trainer to build and progress a lifting program, Pro covers that for $23.99 a year or $74.99 once.

Can Hevy track running?

Hevy logs cardio with time and distance, and Trainer can add cardio to a program, but we didn't find running plans that build toward a race, or GPS run tracking, so you'd pair it with a running app. Kiron's running programs share a calendar with your lifting, though it doesn't show pace.

Can I import a ChatGPT workout plan into Hevy?

We didn't find a way to paste one into the Hevy app. You can type it in as routines, or type @hevy in ChatGPT to have ChatGPT build a plan and save it to your Hevy account. Kiron takes the plan you already have, pasted or photographed. Our ChatGPT plan guide covers asking for a good plan and checking it first.

If you'd rather follow a plan than manage one, or your week includes runs, try Kiron. Pick a program or paste the one you follow, bring your Hevy history, and the next workout will be ready whenever you are. {{kiron:cta-sentence}} Get Kiron.

Still comparing? See how Strong compares, how Fitbod compares, or our guide to workout apps for following a program.
